sketches.title: Pipe Dreams
sketches.premise: You are a talking pipe in a ridiculous underground kingdom. Each turn, install one plumbing part that handles the problem created by the last part; make the system work, not merely look tougher. The Judge decides whether your part actually solves the standing fault.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing part when it directly repairs, redirects, seals, cleans, or safely controls the problem it creates; merely surviving a leak, avoiding the flow, adding a larger copy, or naming a cousin from the same pipe family loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one installed plumbing part and its action in one sentence: “I am a shutoff valve; I stop the cracked pipe’s flood before the basement becomes a swimming pool.”
sketches.first_card: I am a cracked water pipe, spraying everywhere.

sketches.title: Drain Train
sketches.premise: A filthy blockage is traveling through a house drain, and you must send the next plumbing tool to defeat what is currently in its way. Every move is a standing tool acting on the last obstacle, so the chain should feel like practical plumbing rather than magical hand-waving. The Judge rules whether the next tool genuinely clears the route.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing obstacle by breaking, dissolving, gripping, flushing, filtering, or carrying it away; dodging the blockage, merely enduring it, or offering a bigger blockage or a same-family lump loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one plumbing tool or material and say exactly what it does: “I am a drain snake; I coil into the hair clog and pull the disgusting nest free.”
sketches.first_card: I am a wad of hair clogging the drain.

sketches.title: Pressure Court
sketches.premise: Welcome to the grand trial of the pipes: each turn, one plumbing condition makes a demand, and the next fixture or device must answer it. The courtroom advances from the standing pressure problem, not from what anyone hoped would happen. The Judge decides whether the answer controls the pressure in a believable way.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing condition when it reduces, releases, measures, redirects, or safely contains its pressure; merely hiding from it, tolerating it, or using a bigger version of the same pressure loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one plumbing device and its ruling: “I am a pressure regulator; I tame the water hammer before the pipes start applauding with a concussion.”
sketches.first_card: I am water hammer, slamming through the pipes.

sketches.title: Fixture Fight
sketches.premise: Every turn summons one household plumbing fixture to defeat the job performed by the previous fixture. A sink, toilet, shower, hose, or pipe must act on what stands and make the next practical move in the household chain. The Judge decides whether the fixture’s job truly counters the last one.
sketches.criterion: A fixture beats the standing fixture when its normal use directly drains, supplies, washes, catches, redirects, or stops what the other does; merely being larger, nearby, or from the same bathroom family loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name a fixture and its action: “I am a floor drain; I catch the shower’s runaway water before it baptizes the hallway.”
sketches.first_card: I am a shower, pouring water onto the floor.

sketches.title: Pipe Puzzle
sketches.premise: You are building a route through a bizarre plumbing maze one piece at a time. Each new piece must overcome the exact trouble caused by the piece before it, turning bends, traps, pumps, filters, and drains into a working path. The Judge rejects decorative nonsense and rewards a clear mechanical answer.
sketches.criterion: A piece beats the standing piece when it connects, turns, seals, filters, lifts, vents, or releases its consequence; a detour that never handles the trouble, a tougher copy, or a related pipe fitting without a mechanism loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one pipe piece and explain its mechanism: “I am a vent pipe; I let trapped air escape the P-trap so the drain stops gulping like a drunk duck.”
sketches.first_card: I am a sealed pipe bend, trapping air and water.

sketches.title: Plumber of Doom
sketches.premise: The house is collapsing into plumbing chaos, and each turn you become one emergency repair that must defeat the disaster currently standing before you. Your repair remains a real plumbing object or action, not a vague spell or a past event. The Judge decides whether it fixes, blocks, or safely redirects the disaster.
sketches.criterion: A repair beats the standing disaster by sealing, clamping, pumping, shutting, clearing, or containing it; fleeing, merely lasting longer, making a bigger disaster, or offering a related object without a working mechanism loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one emergency repair and its effect: “I am a pipe clamp, crushing the split shut before the leak turns the ceiling into modern art.”
sketches.first_card: I am a burst pipe, flooding the upstairs ceiling.
